sections.title: How does the Alcohol units calculator work?
sections.html:
The Alcohol units calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports alcohol units in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (your country); then you type in the low alcohol beer/cider (Popular beverages), the low alcohol beer/cider (Popular beverages), the standard beer/cider (Popular beverages) and the standard beer/cider (Popular beverages).

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Alcohol units calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Alcohol units=(your country × (alcohol units part 1 + alcohol units part 2))
Standard glass of wine (175 ml)=(10 ÷ 21) × alcohol units part 1 − 6 ÷ 7 × glass of champagne (150 ml) − 10 ÷ 7 × large glass of wine (250 ml) − 11 ÷ 35 × low alcohol beer ÷ cider − 11 ÷ 35 × low alcohol beer ÷ cider − 5 ÷ 7 × small glass of wine (125 ml) − 11 ÷ 14 × standard beer ÷ cider − 11 ÷ 14 × standard beer ÷ cider − 99 ÷ 70 × strong beer ÷ cider − 99 ÷ 70 × strong beer ÷ cider
Rum & cola=(40 ÷ 133) × alcohol units part 2 − 44 ÷ 133 × alcopop (275 ml) − 40 ÷ 133 × custom drink alcohol units − 36 ÷ 133 × fortified wine, 50 ml − 18 ÷ 19 × margarita − 31 ÷ 19 × martini − 21 ÷ 19 × mojito − 64 ÷ 133 × shot of spirit (single, 25 ml) − 15 ÷ 19 × vodka & tonic
Drink volume=10 × custom drink alcohol units ÷ drink proof

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • UK beer sizes, opening in 568 ml
  • UK beer sizes, opening in 330 ml
  • UK beer sizes, opening in 440 ml
  • UK beer sizes, opening in 330 ml
  • UK beer sizes, opening in 1000 ml
  • UK beer sizes, opening in 330 ml
  • Volume, opening in milliliters
  • %, opening in percent

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Alcohol units calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the low alcohol beer/cider, the standard beer/cider and the strong beer/cider — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Alcohol units calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns alcohol units, derived from the low alcohol beer/cider, the standard beer/cider and the strong beer/cider. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Alcohol units calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the low alcohol beer/cider, the standard beer/cider and the strong beer/cider, which is 22 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter low alcohol beer/cider (Popular beverages) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Low alcohol beer/cider (Popular beverages) opens in 568 ml and the chip beside it offers 4 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Custom drink alcohol units = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Alcohol units calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
